programs.name: Mississippi veterans: county veterans service officers for claims help
programs.organization: County veterans service officers; Mississippi Veterans Affairs
programs.description: Free help with VA claims, pension and survivor benefits from county veterans service officers, who are certified each year by the Mississippi State Veterans Affairs Board. Every county has one. Mississippi Veterans Affairs’ Veterans Benefits Specialists also work from offices across the state and at the Jackson VA Medical Center.
programs.next_step: Choose your county for its service officer. Mississippi Veterans Affairs’ main office in Jackson is at 601-576-4850.
constraints: Call before you go; many county offices are staffed part of the week.

sources.title: Mississippi Veterans Affairs: Service Officers
sources.scope: Main office, Veterans Benefits Specialist offices and the 82 county service officers with address and phone; read in full.

programs.name: Mississippi Access to Care (MAC) Centers
programs.organization: Mississippi Department of Human Services, Division of Aging and Adult Services
programs.description: Mississippi Access to Care Centers are a free source of objective information about programs and services for older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers, including long-term care options and Medicaid waiver screening. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 844-822-4622, or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

sources.title: Mississippi Department of Human Services: State Plan on Aging, FFY 2023 update

programs.name: Medicare counseling (SHIP) for Mississippi
programs.organization: Mississippi Department of Human Services, State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP)
programs.description: Free, unbiased Medicare counseling from Mississippi’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, run by the Division of Aging and Adult Services with the Area Agencies on Aging and the MAC network: plan choices, enrollment, costs and help paying for Medicare.
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

sources.title: Mississippi Department of Human Services: SHIP provides free and unbiased Medicare guidance
sources.scope: SHIP run with the Area Agencies on Aging and the MAC network; call 1-844-822-4622; search excerpt.

programs.name: Mississippi Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: Mississippi Department of Human Services, Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
programs.description: Independent advocacy for residents of nursing homes and assisted living, through local ombudsmen at the Area Agencies on Aging.
programs.next_step: Call the ombudsman help line at 888-844-0041. To report abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable adult at home, call the 24-hour Adult Protective Services hotline, 844-437-6282. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

programs.name: Free legal help for Mississippi veterans and older adults
programs.organization: Mississippi Center for Legal Services; North Mississippi Rural Legal Services
programs.description: Mississippi’s legal services programs give free civil legal help to people with low incomes and, through the Area Agencies on Aging, to older adults. Mississippi Center for Legal Services serves central, east-central and south Mississippi; North Mississippi Rural Legal Services serves the north and the Delta. In the southwest counties, older adults are referred to a contracted law firm in Tylertown.
programs.next_step: Call 800-498-1804. In the north and the Delta, North Mississippi Rural Legal Services’ Oxford office is at 662-234-8731; in the Jackson area, Mississippi Center for Legal Services is at 601-948-6752.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income and case type; no criminal cases.

sources.title: Mississippi Department of Human Services: Legal Assistance Help Guide (undated)
sources.scope: Each legal provider’s office, phones and the counties it serves for older adults; read in full.

programs.name: VA health care systems serving Mississippi
programs.description: Mississippi veterans are served mainly by VA Jackson health care (G.V. (Sonny) Montgomery VA Medical Center, 1500 E. Woodrow Wilson Avenue, Jackson; 601-362-4471, with clinics in Columbus, Greenville, Hattiesburg, Kosciusko, McComb, Meridian and Natchez) and the VA Gulf Coast Veterans Health Care System (400 Veterans Avenue, Biloxi; 228-523-5000).
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic; northern counties may be closer to another system. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 82 counties have a county veterans service officer, an Area Agency on Aging (ten agencies) and the statewide long-term care ombudsman line. Six LIFE of Mississippi independent living offices cover 78 counties; Calhoun, Choctaw, Union and Webster are not listed by any office in the national directory.
coverage_note: County veterans service officers come from Mississippi Veterans Affairs’ Service Officers page. Area Agencies on Aging come from the Mississippi Department of Human Services’ State Plan on Aging. The long-term care ombudsman help line comes from the department’s ombudsman page. Independent living offices come from the ILRU national directory. Reviewed November 16, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
